research.report:
**Accenture — AI & Data Graduate Programme FY28**

All linked sources were accessed **12 September 2026**. “Saved JD” refers to the supplied description recorded that date; no local files or candidate information were accessed.

**Posting verification and conditions**

The Ireland graduate programme’s AI & Data link resolves to the exact supplied posting. Its live metadata confirms Strategy & Consulting Ireland, Dublin, permanent full-time employment, €40,000 annually, an “Onsite” classification and a 25 October 2026 deadline. [Specific posting](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/postings/5d2e98e6-2568-4833-bb13-8a067bf55d18) (accessed 12 September 2026).

The application page is accessible and displays CV upload and submission controls. However, the extracted posting contains empty detailed-JD sections, and the form’s substantive questions are missing. Availability is therefore verified at page level; successful submission was not tested. [Application form](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/postings/5d2e98e6-2568-4833-bb13-8a067bf55d18/applications/new) (accessed 12 September 2026).

**Saved-JD facts, not independently reverified:** starts September 2027–Spring 2028; bachelor results required before joining; minimum predicted/obtained 2.1 and Level 8 honours bachelor/equivalent; final-year/recent-graduate eligibility. Attendance is described as at least 1–2 office/client days weekly, potentially five, with domestic/international travel. The form reportedly requests full-time Irish work-rights evidence and warns that AI-assisted applications may be withdrawn. These details retain the supplied 12 September 2026 date caveat; the work-rights question does not establish sponsorship policy.

**Role mission and business domain**

**Explicit:** The graduate stream collects and analyses client data, applies quantitative/statistical techniques, combines AI with analytics and automation, and implements cloud-data solutions. [Ireland graduate programme](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/graduate-programmes-ireland) (accessed 12 September 2026). The saved JD adds AI strategy, commercial use cases, process improvement and adoption.

Accenture describes its business as enterprise solutions and services spanning strategy, consulting, technology and operations, supported by industry expertise and technology partnerships. [Accenture–Mistral announcement](https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2026/accenture-and-mistral-ai-accelerate-enterprise-reinvention-with-scalable-ai-that-delivers-strategic-autonomy-for-customers) (accessed 12 September 2026).

**Inference:** The mission is to translate business problems into useful data and AI outcomes: understand a process, establish evidence, support a solution and help people adopt it. Commercial value, explainability and communication likely matter alongside technical execution. No particular industry or research specialism is guaranteed. Employer guidance says assignments depend on client demand and some graduates start on internal projects. [Ireland support hub](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/en/support-hub-ireland) (accessed 12 September 2026).

**Proposed 30/60/90-day outcomes — inference, not employer commitments**

These are reasonable review milestones derived from the programme’s analysis/cloud-delivery remit and published induction, case-study and workplace training. [Programme and training](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/graduate-programmes-ireland) (accessed 12 September 2026).

| Timing | Plausible outcome | Reviewable evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 30 days | Complete induction; understand the assignment, users, data access and success measures | Learning plan, problem statement, stakeholder map and initial data-quality assessment |
| 60 days | Deliver a supervised analysis or prototype addressing one agreed question | Reproducible analysis, dashboard, pipeline or AI prototype; baseline comparison and documented limitations |
| 90 days | Own a bounded deliverable through feedback and handover | Tested output, concise client presentation, operating notes and recommended next steps |

Production deployment or quantified savings within 90 days should not be presumed; assignment scope and access would determine feasibility.

**Relevant projects and recent initiatives**

- **Irish AI-adoption study, July 2026 — government-confirmed:** Accenture was commissioned to investigate adoption opportunities, barriers and policy supports across manufacturing, tourism, construction and ICT services. Findings were intended to inform Ireland’s sectoral AI strategy. **Relevance inferred:** research synthesis, business interviews, use-case evaluation and adoption recommendations closely resemble the role’s consulting remit. Graduate participation is unknown. [Department announcement, 15 July 2026](https://enterprise.gov.ie/en/news-and-events/department-news/2026/july/minister-niamh-smyth-calls-on-businesses-to-shape-ireland-s-future-ai-strategy.html) (accessed 12 September 2026).
- **Mistral collaboration, February 2026 — announced initiative:** The partnership targets enterprise AI deployment, governance and regional requirements, with planned training and change-management support. **Relevance inferred:** successful AI delivery involves operating models and user capability as well as models. This is not evidence of a particular Dublin assignment or completed rollout. [Accenture announcement, 26 February 2026](https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2026/accenture-and-mistral-ai-accelerate-enterprise-reinvention-with-scalable-ai-that-delivers-strategic-autonomy-for-customers) (accessed 12 September 2026).
- **Google Cloud client delivery, October 2025 — employer-reported:** JCOM’s JAICO project uses Gemini to summarise customer-service conversations. Radisson used Vertex AI, Gemini and BigQuery for multilingual advertising personalisation. Accenture also announced expanded agentic capabilities in its joint Google Cloud centre. **Relevance inferred:** these illustrate connected data preparation, AI implementation, workflow improvement and commercial evaluation. No connection to this intake is established. [Client examples, 9 October 2025](https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2025/accenture-helps-organizations-advance-agentic-ai-with-gemini-enterprise) (accessed 12 September 2026).

**Technical stack: requirements versus inference**

| Evidence category | Technologies and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Explicitly sought in saved JD | Familiarity with a relevant combination of GenAI/agentic AI, cloud platforms, Python/R or other data languages, ML, SQL/ETL/NoSQL/warehousing and BI. All areas are expressly not expected; no individual tool is established as universally mandatory. |
| Independently verified programme content | Statistical modelling, analytics, automation and cloud-data implementation; training includes Excel/data visualisation and PowerPoint/storytelling. These training topics are not stated entry requirements. |
| Company-used, not role-required | Google Cloud, Gemini, Vertex AI and BigQuery appear in cited client projects. Mistral AI Studio appears in the announced partnership. Exposure is possible, not promised. |
| Inferred working practices | Reproducible analysis, data-quality checks, version control, model evaluation and documentation would support reliable delivery. Specific frameworks, cloud provider, BI vendor and deployment tooling remain unknown. |

Public evidence: [Graduate programme](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/graduate-programmes-ireland), [Google client projects](https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2025/accenture-helps-organizations-advance-agentic-ai-with-gemini-enterprise), [Mistral partnership](https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2026/accenture-and-mistral-ai-accelerate-enterprise-reinvention-with-scalable-ai-that-delivers-strategic-autonomy-for-customers) (all accessed 12 September 2026).

**Skills, deliverables and relationships**

**Saved-JD expectations:** structured thinking, business curiosity, clear communication, adaptability, initiative, creativity and teamwork/leadership examples.

**Inferred deliverables:** use-case assessments, process maps, data analyses, prototypes, dashboards, presentations and adoption materials. Depending on assignment, likely collaborators include client process owners, data specialists, engineers, business users and an Accenture delivery lead. These are functional relationships, not a verified team structure. A People Lead supporting development and learning is explicitly described in the [Ireland support hub](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/en/support-hub-ireland) (accessed 12 September 2026).

**Seniority and interview evidence**

This is an entry-level graduate pathway; the programme explicitly welcomes final-year students and recent graduates. No professional-experience minimum or formal career level was verified. [Graduate programme](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/graduate-programmes-ireland) (accessed 12 September 2026).

The Ireland hub describes application → Discovery Portal → virtual assessment centre → Senior Manager/Managing Director interview. It mentions strengths, decision-making, paired/immersive exercises and demonstrating educational technical skills. [Ireland recruitment guidance](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/en/support-hub-ireland) (accessed 12 September 2026).

A separate employer page describes an approximately 60-minute, usually face-to-face business interview with two technology-oriented scenarios and strengths discussion; it explicitly says successful AI & Data applicants proceed to technical interviews. Its applicability to this Irish intake needs confirmation because format differs from Ireland’s guidance. No FY28 coding-test platform or technical syllabus is established. [Business interview guidance](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/strengths-based-interview) (accessed 12 September 2026).

**Inference:** useful assessment evidence would demonstrate clear problem decomposition, personal contribution, technical reasoning, limitations and business implications—not merely familiarity with tool names.

**Unresolved questions**

Confirm the intake-specific interview sequence and technical format; start-date allocation; accepted degree equivalencies and sponsorship; first-assignment selection; coding-versus-strategy balance; team/reporting structure; cloud/BI stack; training allocation; attendance and travel expectations; and initial performance measures.

advice.summary: For Accenture’s Dublin AI & Data Graduate Programme FY28, the strongest resume would demonstrate graduate eligibility, structured business problem-solving, credible technical work and clear communication. A relevant combination of skills matters more than covering every technology. This is advisory research only; the saved form reportedly discourages AI-assisted applications, so this report should not be submitted as application text.
advice.report:
The expected resume should show an emerging consultant who can connect data and AI work to a business decision. No candidate information was supplied, so all recommendations below describe evidence to seek, not skills or achievements the candidate possesses.

**Prioritized resume evidence**

1. **Eligibility and education.** Clearly state degree, institution, graduation date and accurately labelled obtained or predicted classification. The saved JD specifies a minimum 2.1, Level 8 honours bachelor/equivalent, final-year/recent-graduate eligibility and results before starting. These details rely on the saved description dated 12 September 2026; they were not independently reverified in the supplied live extraction. [Exact posting](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/postings/5d2e98e6-2568-4833-bb13-8a067bf55d18), publication date unavailable; supplied access date 12 September 2026.
2. **One or two substantial analytical projects.** Prioritize a clear business question, data preparation, an appropriate analytical method, evaluation and a recommendation. Coursework, dissertations and independent projects can provide this evidence; professional experience is not established as mandatory.
3. **Communication and collaboration.** Include verifiable examples of explaining findings, resolving ambiguity, responding to feedback and contributing to team decisions. Separate individual work from the team’s output. Extracurricular examples are relevant because the saved application explicitly requests them.
4. **Technical depth supported by artifacts.** Connect each prominent skill to a repository, notebook, dashboard, report or demonstrable implementation. A short, supported skills list is more persuasive than an unexplained catalogue.
5. **Initiative and adoption.** Where supported, show how a problem was identified, a solution tested with users and instructions or a handover produced. These support the saved JD’s process-improvement and AI-adoption remit.

Dublin attendance, travel and work authorization should be answered accurately where requested. Supporting identity or work-rights documents belong in the appropriate application process, not a public portfolio. Sponsorship policy remains unknown.

**Essential versus useful skills**

**Explicit expectations:** structured thinking, business curiosity, communication, adaptability, initiative, creativity and teamwork/leadership examples. Relevant technical familiarity is sought across some combination of GenAI/agentic AI, cloud, Python/R or another data language, ML, SQL/data engineering and BI. The saved JD expressly does not expect all areas; no individual language, cloud provider or BI product is established as universally mandatory.

**Inferred priorities:** a coherent combination such as Python plus SQL plus visualization would support the programme’s stated analytics and cloud-data work. Reproducibility, data-quality checks, baseline comparisons and documentation would strengthen credibility. These are advisory expectations, not additional entry requirements. [Ireland graduate programme](https://accenture.pinpointhq.com/graduate-programmes-ireland), publication date unavailable; supplied access date 12 September 2026.

**Useful differentiators:** evaluated AI prototypes, basic cloud implementation and adoption materials. Accenture’s Google announcement describes JCOM conversation summarization and Radisson advertising personalization; its Mistral partnership addresses enterprise AI deployment, governance and training. These establish company context, not the Dublin intake’s assigned stack. [Google announcement](https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2025/accenture-helps-organizations-advance-agentic-ai-with-gemini-enterprise), published 9 October 2025; [Mistral announcement](https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2026/accenture-and-mistral-ai-accelerate-enterprise-reinvention-with-scalable-ai-that-delivers-strategic-autonomy-for-customers), published 26 February 2026; both supplied access dates 12 September 2026.

Before listing a skill, retain evidence of using it and be able to explain design choices, failures and limitations. A course certificate supports training completion; a tested implementation supports practical familiarity. Claim cloud deployment only with an actual deployment and operating evidence. Claim leadership only with identifiable responsibility and contribution.

**Proposed projects to build — not completed candidate experience**

**1. Irish sector AI-adoption decision brief.** Accenture was commissioned to examine AI adoption across manufacturing, tourism, construction and ICT services. [Government announcement](https://enterprise.gov.ie/en/news-and-events/department-news/2026/july/minister-niamh-smyth-calls-on-businesses-to-shape-ireland-s-future-ai-strategy.html), published 15 July 2026; supplied access date 12 September 2026.

Scope: choose one sector and assess three bounded AI use cases against data readiness, feasibility, adoption barriers and potential value. Use publicly available enterprise AI-use statistics from [Eurostat dataset isoc_eb_ai](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/isoc_eb_ai/default/table?lang=en), supplemented by relevant [CSO PxStat](https://data.cso.ie/) tables. Confirm sector coverage, survey definitions and release dates before analysis; detailed Irish sector breakdowns may be unavailable.

Tools: Python or R, SQL where useful, and Power BI or another visualization tool. Evaluate missingness, comparability and sensitivity of use-case rankings to scoring weights. Aggregate adoption figures cannot establish firm-level returns or causal barriers.

Feasible deliverable: a reproducible analysis, a small dashboard and a five-slide decision brief with a proposed pilot and adoption plan. Business value is decision support: transparent prioritization and testable assumptions. Any savings calculation must be labelled a scenario with explicit inputs.

Resume evidence needed: completed artifacts, source/version log, scoring rationale, reproducible results and documented personal contribution. Stakeholder validation requires actual feedback; do not imply participation in Accenture’s commissioned study.

**2. Customer-service narrative summarization prototype.** Inspired by the JCOM example in the October 2025 Google announcement, build a small summarization and issue-routing workflow using published narratives from the [CFPB Consumer Complaint Database](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/). These are US financial complaints, not call transcripts or JCOM data; the domain and format mismatch must remain explicit.

Scope: use a manageable sample, create a manually reviewed held-out evaluation set and compare a simple extractive baseline with one language-model approach. Tools could include Python, SQLite and a local model or permitted model API. Avoid unnecessary personal details and review dataset usage terms.

Evaluate factual consistency, omitted critical facts, routing accuracy, latency and cost. Test invented details and prompt-like content inside narratives. A small timed reviewer study can assess review effort; without one, do not claim time savings.

Feasible deliverable: a runnable demo, evaluation table, error analysis and human-review handover guide. Business relevance is more consistent triage and potentially lower review effort, subject to testing.

Resume evidence needed: working code, model/version records, evaluation rubric, held-out results and reproducible baseline comparisons. Measured prototype performance must not be presented as production impact, client delivery or an Accenture engagement.

For either project, describe the problem, personal contribution, method, measured result and limitation. Distinguish observed results from projected financial outcomes. Neither proposed project belongs on a resume as completed work before it is built and evaluated.

research.report:
# KPMG Tax Technology - public company research

Research date: 12 September 2026. Separate public-research worker; no candidate context supplied.

KPMG Ireland's Tax Transformation & Technology service describes helping clients meet reporting demands, manage compliance costs and improve finance/tax information. Source-system analysis, tax master data and system logic, information quality across IT and finance, and preventative/detective controls are explicit service areas. This is a client-service offering, not a claim that KPMG itself has failing systems.

Source: [KPMG Tax Transformation & Technology](https://kpmg.com/ie/en/services/tax/tax-transformation-and-technology.html), accessed 12 September 2026.

The official STEM careers page identifies digital tax reporting, ERP optimisation, compliance automation, dashboards, robotics and GenAI as possible Tax Technology activities. Python, Power Automate and Alteryx appear as possible learning/work technologies, not universal mandatory entry skills.

Source: [KPMG STEM opportunities](https://kpmg.com/ie/en/careers/stem-opportunities.html), accessed 12 September 2026.

## Interpretation

Reliable data, traceable exceptions, practical automation and communication between technical and finance colleagues are plausible graduate contribution areas. Specific client assignments, tax advisory responsibility and guaranteed use of particular tools are not established.

The research worker could not retrieve the Avature description independently. The main task read the complete employer JD and matching application gateway in the browser. The employer vacancy list's 21 October 2026, 17:00 closing date supersedes the older aggregator's September date.

# KPMG Tax Technology Graduate Programme 2027 — evaluation

Job ID: `1acf78884105297f` · Reviewed 12 September 2026.

**Decision:** credible graduate analytics/BI opportunity within target scope; administrative eligibility remains unresolved. Do not assert that all entry conditions are met. This is a separate active-profile comparison against the independent hiring benchmark, not a prediction of selection.

## Requirements and evidence

- **Current master's student — supported by the active record:** `EDU-MSC-001` records the MSc programme in Data Science at MTU as in progress (Sep 2025–Sep 2026). The planned end month does not establish an award; exact award title remains unresolved.
- **On track for minimum 2.1 — conditional, not confirmed:** the only MSc result is Semester 1: 2:1. There is no verified predicted or final degree result. `EDU-BTECH-001` reports 9.4/10, but its Irish classification/equivalence must not be inferred. Obtain appropriate prediction/result or employer equivalence confirmation before answering this condition affirmatively.
- **Initiative and learning — supported:** `PROJ-NIQ-REPORTING` documents learning the proprietary platform within two weeks and delivering 300+ reports over six months. `PROJ-NIQ-POC` supports building a reusable finance-dashboard prototype from a client wireframe; efficiency estimates remain user-reported.
- **Communication and teamwork — supported:** NielsenIQ BRD clarification with client stakeholders, `SKILL-DELIVERY-001`, and the three-person executive-dashboard demonstration/handover (`PROJ-AZ-EXEC`) provide concrete evidence.

Professional work is BI delivery; Python/ML evidence remains academic or project-based.
- **Client-facing motivation — partially evidenced:** prior client delivery supports readiness, but personal motivation for tax technology and professional study needs a truthful application/interview explanation.
- **Tax-domain knowledge — gap, not a stated mandatory entry barrier:** no professional tax advice, tax compliance, ERP tax configuration, ACA/tax qualification or Alteryx experience is established. The JD accepts any discipline and offers development; research examples do not create extra mandatory tools or candidate skills.

## Exactly one selected project

Select **`PROJ-AZ-RECON` — Finance Access Reconciliation Dashboard**, a professional AstraZeneca team project. Five-source consolidation and drill-through to access requests/discrepancies directly illustrate traceability, information quality and coordination around finance processes. research.report:
**Arup — Data Scientist Work Placement, Dublin**

Research date: **11 September 2026**. Explicit facts below come from employer sources; proposed outcomes and working practices are labelled as inferences.

**Posting verification and role mission**

The employer page matches the supplied title, Dublin location and requisition **IRE0000HN**. It displays an **Apply for Job** control and no closure notice. The description substantively matches the supplied snapshot, whose stated verification date was 8 September 2026. The application submission workflow was not tested. [Employer posting](https://jobs.arup.com/jobs/data-scientist-work-placement-34369) (accessed 2026-09-11).

**Explicit:** The intern joins Data Insights, working alongside data scientists/analysts on solutions for internal and external clients. Its domain spans buildings, transport, sustainability, energy and water. [Employer posting](https://jobs.arup.com/jobs/data-scientist-work-placement-34369) (accessed 2026-09-11).

**Interpretation:** The mission is to turn imperfect project data into useful evidence for engineering and operational decisions. Dashboard development and preparation of usable data appear at least as central as modelling; the advert does not establish a research-heavy AI role.

**Proposed 30/60/90-day outcomes — inference, not Arup commitments**

These outcomes assume a placement lasting at least three months. They translate the supplied JD into reviewable deliverables and reflect Arup’s wider emphasis on appropriate analytical methods, data quality and usable products. [Data and AI services](https://www.arup.com/services/data-and-artificial-intelligence/) (accessed 2026-09-11).

| Period | Plausible outcome | Evidence of completion |
|---|---|---|
| First 30 days | Understand one project’s decision, users and data; reproduce an existing analysis | Agreed problem statement, data dictionary, quality checks and initial Python/SQL preparation workflow |
| By 60 days | Deliver a bounded analytical prototype | Cleaned dataset, dashboard or baseline model; documented assumptions; review with an analyst and domain specialist |
| By 90 days | Refine and hand over a useful output | Reproducible workflow, validated calculations, user feedback, concise findings and handover documentation |

Success should be judged by whether an output supports a decision and can be trusted and maintained. No numerical performance targets are published for this placement.

**Business and domain**

Arup’s Irish operation combines building and infrastructure design, digital insights and strategic advice, with offices in Cork, Dublin, Galway and Limerick. This places the role inside a multidisciplinary consultancy serving built-environment clients. [Arup Ireland](https://www.arup.com/contact-us/ireland/) (accessed 2026-09-11).

Its data practice describes work from requirements gathering through deployed products, including stand-alone statistical analysis where sufficient. It stresses quality, assurance, human accountability and explainability in technical and safety-critical settings. [Data and AI services](https://www.arup.com/services/data-and-artificial-intelligence/) (accessed 2026-09-11).

**Inference:** Analysts need to understand what measurements mean physically, how data were collected and what uncertainty permits a client to conclude. A technically correct model can still be unhelpful if its metric does not answer the engineering question.

**Relevant projects and recent initiatives**

These are evidence of Arup’s work, **not confirmed assignments for this intern**.

- **Ireland: TII Intelligent Transport Systems.** Arup documents a five-year engagement covering strategy, deployment, pilots, technical advice and asset management. Traffic information from cameras and counters supports journey-time reporting and longer-term planning. The case study is undated, so it should not be represented as a newly awarded 2026 project. **Relevance inferred:** operational data quality, time-based analysis and communicating transport performance. [TII project](https://www.arup.com/projects/tii-intelligent-transport-systems-strategy-and-implementation/) (accessed 2026-09-11).
- **Hong Kong: AI-enabled public-building design, 2 September 2026.** Arup announced two additional ArchSD commissions for long-span structural and piled-foundation design platforms, extending an existing architectural platform. The work combines engineering optimisation, data analytics and agentic workflows. **Relevance inferred:** illustrates how analytics is embedded in engineering decisions; it does not establish agentic AI as a Dublin placement requirement. [ArchSD announcement](https://www.arup.com/news/bringing-ai-into-the-heart-of-public-building-design-with-archsd-in-hong-kong/) (accessed 2026-09-11).
- **Firm-wide AI policy, April 2026.** Arup sets expectations for approved systems, proportionate assurance, secure data handling, human accountability and lifecycle management. **Relevance inferred:** any modelling contribution would need review and clear limitations. [AI policy](https://www.arup.com/globalassets/downloads/corporate-documents/policies/2026/ai-policy-2026.pdf) (accessed 2026-09-11).

**Technical stack and skills**

| Evidence level | Requirement or implication |
|---|---|
| Explicit | Python and SQL proficiency for analytics |
| Explicit | Dashboard experience using Tableau, Power BI **and/or** AWS QuickSight; all three are not stipulated |
| Explicit | Basic machine-learning understanding; experience cleaning, preparing and transforming data |
| Inferred | Reproducible scripts, validation checks and clear visual explanations are useful delivery practices |
| Unknown | Python libraries, database engine, cloud hosting, version control, deployment tooling and production ownership |

The explicit items are from the [employer posting](https://jobs.arup.com/jobs/data-scientist-work-placement-34369) (accessed 2026-09-11). Naming QuickSight does not establish wider AWS engineering responsibilities. There is no published requirement here for deep learning, LLMs, Spark, GIS or MLOps.

**Deliverables and stakeholder relationships — justified inference**

Likely outputs include prepared datasets, analytical queries/scripts, dashboards, exploratory findings and possibly a simple model. Useful accompanying evidence would include metric definitions, validation results and a short explanation of limitations. This follows the supplied duties and Arup’s public emphasis on user-centred delivery. [Data and AI services](https://www.arup.com/services/data-and-artificial-intelligence/) (accessed 2026-09-11).

The advertised relationships are fellow data scientists/analysts and internal/external clients. A plausible working pattern is analyst review, domain-specialist interpretation and feedback from the people using the results. The reporting manager, team size, client-contact frequency and project allocation are unknown. [Employer posting](https://jobs.arup.com/jobs/data-scientist-work-placement-34369) (accessed 2026-09-11).

**Seniority and interview evidence**

**Explicit:** This is an internship for someone studying computer science, computer engineering, data analytics or equivalent. The advert seeks curiosity, creative problem-solving, adaptability and commitment to sustainable development. It specifies no minimum professional tenure. [Employer posting](https://jobs.arup.com/jobs/data-scientist-work-placement-34369) (accessed 2026-09-11).

Arup’s **2025 early-careers FAQ** describes Ireland applications as online submission, recruiter CV review, shortlisting and hiring-manager review, followed by a maximum of two formal, competency-based interviews. This is older programme-level guidance, not confirmation of this requisition’s process. The PDF’s search-indexed text was accessible; direct opening failed. [Early-careers FAQ](https://careers.arup.com/earlycareers/custom/ARUP_03/resources/files/earlycareersfaqs2025.pdf) (accessed 2026-09-11).

**Inferred interview evidence:** An end-to-end analysis explaining cleaning choices, SQL logic, dashboard design and model evaluation would directly demonstrate the advertised skills. Examples of learning unfamiliar tools, responding to feedback and connecting analysis to sustainability would address the behavioural criteria. A coding test, presentation or assessment centre is **unconfirmed**.

**Unresolved questions**

- What are the start date, duration, weekly hours and university-placement eligibility rules?
- Is the snapshot’s hybrid/full-time designation accurate, and what attendance is expected?
- Which sectors and projects would the intern support, and how is supervision arranged?
- Which dashboard tool, database and Python environment are actually used?
- How much work involves modelling versus preparation and reporting?
- What are the salary, placement-specific benefits, application deadline and interview stages?

These details are not established by the verified posting. Public visibility and the application control support apparent availability, but do not prove the application system will accept a completed submission.

hiring.report:
The JD establishes the requirements below. All suggested evidence standards, projects and interview questions are professional judgment, not additional employer requirements or insider knowledge. Citations refer to the supplied public research; no independent browsing was performed.

**Essential versus desirable evidence**

The JD explicitly seeks someone studying computer science, computer engineering, data analytics or equivalent; Python and SQL proficiency for analytics; dashboard experience in Tableau, Power BI and/or AWS QuickSight; basic machine-learning understanding; and experience preparing, cleaning and transforming data. One listed dashboard tool can satisfy the wording. It also emphasises creative problem-solving, learning, adaptability and sustainable development. No minimum professional experience is stated. [1]

At placement level, convincing depth would mean explaining and adapting work personally completed:

- **Python and preparation:** Load imperfect data, inspect types and distributions, handle missing values and duplicates deliberately, join sources, and check that transformations preserve intended meaning. Explain when a missing reading must remain missing rather than become zero.
- **SQL:** Demonstrate joins, filtering, aggregation and explicit table grain. Explain how a one-to-many join can inflate totals and how to detect it. CTEs or window functions provide useful additional evidence where the problem calls for them.
- **Dashboards:** Build a usable view around a decision, with defined measures, units, filters and understandable comparisons. Reconcile displayed totals to the underlying data and explain why each chart is useful.
- **Basic ML:** Explain a simple regression or classification method, establish a baseline, separate training and evaluation appropriately, and recognise leakage, overfitting and misleading metrics. Advanced architecture knowledge is unnecessary for this evidence standard.
- **Learning and collaboration:** Give a concrete example of learning a tool, incorporating feedback or revising an unsuccessful approach. Team coursework is valid; distinguish individual contributions.
- **Sustainability:** Connect an analysis to resource use, resilience or accessibility while acknowledging trade-offs and uncertainty. Do not equate a predictive improvement with proven environmental impact.

Desirable evidence, by professional judgment, includes reproducible workflows, version control, concise documentation, stakeholder communication and awareness of physical units and measurement limitations. Arup's public data practice stresses quality, assurance and explainability, supporting this emphasis. [2] GIS, cloud engineering, deep learning, LLMs and production MLOps are not stated requirements. QuickSight does not imply a requirement for broader AWS expertise.

The role remains accessible through student work. The wording says “studying”; eligibility for someone who has already graduated is unresolved, rather than automatically established or excluded. [1]

**Portfolio options — choose one or two, not all**

These are bounded learning projects, not proposed unpaid deliverables for Arup. Use public, licensed or clearly labelled synthetic data. None is a confirmed placement assignment.

1. **Building energy: identify periods worth investigating.**
   - **Decision and access:** Help a facilities user prioritise unusually high consumption. Assume access to an openly licensed hourly electricity dataset for one building and compatible public weather observations. If occupancy is unavailable, state that limitation; do not imply access to Arup/client data.
   - **Scope:** Analyse a few months, clean timestamps and meter gaps, aggregate with SQL, and compare a seasonal baseline with a simple weather-based regression using Python.
   - **Deliverables:** Data dictionary, reproducible preparation script, SQL queries, one dashboard in a listed tool and a short findings note.
   - **Validation:** Report missing-period rates and energy-total reconciliation; use a chronological holdout and compare MAE against the baseline. Inspect errors by hour and weekday. Without labelled faults, describe anomalies as investigation candidates.
   - **Explain decisions:** Justify units, treatment of gaps, baseline choice and alert thresholds. Explain why unusual consumption does not prove waste or establish achievable savings.

2. **Transport monitoring: distinguish traffic change from sensor failure.**
   - **Decision and access:** Help a transport analyst assess recurring peak demand and monitoring coverage. Assume a downloadable, licensed traffic-counter dataset with timestamps, locations and counts; confirm its coverage before choosing the analysis. If only counts exist, do not claim to measure journey reliability.
   - **Scope:** Select a small set of locations and several weeks. Profile missing intervals, duplicate records and implausible counts; compare weekday and weekend patterns in SQL and Python.
   - **Deliverables:** Quality report, documented aggregation queries, a Power BI/Tableau/QuickSight dashboard and a one-page interpretation.
   - **Validation:** Measure valid-interval coverage, reconcile daily totals and test filters. For synthetic injected outages, report detection precision and recall separately from findings on real data.
   - **Explain decisions:** Distinguish zero traffic from absent readings, justify exclusion rules and show whether conclusions change under different coverage thresholds. Arup's published TII work makes transport monitoring a relevant business illustration, not evidence of an intern assignment. [3]

3. **Water demand: produce a transparent short-term forecast.**
   - **Decision and access:** Support a hypothetical operator's near-term planning. Assume an openly licensed daily demand series; otherwise use clearly labelled synthetic data solely to demonstrate the workflow.
   - **Scope:** Use one service area, compare a seasonal-naive forecast with a simple regression, and visualise forecast errors. Avoid operational control recommendations.
   - **Deliverables:** Preparation pipeline, baseline comparison, dashboard and brief handover explaining update steps and limitations.
   - **Validation:** Use rolling time-based evaluation; report MAE and error on high-demand days. Check missing dates and physically impossible values. Synthetic results cannot establish real operational performance.
   - **Explain decisions:** Justify forecast horizon, feature availability at prediction time and the relative costs of under- and overprediction. Explain what additional evidence would be needed before operational use. Water is an explicitly advertised sector. [1]

**Interview questions and strong-answer signals**

These are suggested preparation questions, not confirmed Arup interview content.

- **“Walk me from a raw dataset to a useful decision.”** Strong answers define the user, data grain, quality problems, transformations, checks and limitations; they identify personal contributions.
- **“A join doubles your reported consumption. What happened?”** Look for examination of key uniqueness, join cardinality, before/after counts and totals, followed by a fix grounded in the intended grain.
- **“Your model beats a baseline under a random split. Is that enough?”** Strong answers consider time dependence, repeated entities, leakage, future feature availability and evaluation that reflects intended use.
- **“How would you improve a dashboard that users misunderstand?”** Look for clarifying the decision, checking metric definitions, simplifying visuals and testing interpretation with users.
- **“An engineer challenges your finding. What do you do?”** Strong answers inspect assumptions and measurement meaning, seek domain context and revise conclusions when warranted. Arup's public emphasis on human accountability supports this approach. [2, 4]
- **“Describe learning something unfamiliar or changing direction.”** A specific student example showing initiative, feedback and reflection is sufficient; prestige or project size is secondary.

**Weak evidence and presentation**

Common weaknesses include unexplained tutorial copies, tool lists without outputs, dashboards without defined measures, model scores without baselines, and cleaning that silently drops inconvenient records. Red flags include fabricated client work, overstated team contributions, presenting synthetic data as real, or claiming causal savings from correlations.

For a resume, identify student/personal/team context and use concise bullets covering the problem, personal action, method and measured result. Report only observed metrics: dataset coverage, checks passed or held-out performance are legitimate; hypothetical financial or carbon benefits must remain hypothetical.

Link to a readable README, selected dashboard screenshots, key queries and an explanation of validation. Include dataset provenance, access instructions, assumptions and a short account of one decision you changed after checking evidence. One coherent project is stronger than numerous unfinished demonstrations.

| Essential requirement | Assessment | Specific active profile IDs and evidence boundaries |
|---|---|---|
| Studying a relevant degree | Partial; placement eligibility unknown | EDU-MSC-001 and personal:current_status report current MSc study at MTU, September 2025–September 2026. EDU-MSC-001 is conditional: use “MSc programme in Data Science, in progress” pending exact award-title confirmation. EDU-BTECH-001 supplies a completed Computer Science degree, but does not establish current student eligibility. Confirm status at the placement start date. |
| Python proficiency for analytics | Supported through academic work | PROJ-MSC-FRAUD, PROJ-FAANG-PCA and PROJ-SECOM-FAULT-DETECTION describe substantial analytical workflows; SKILL-ACADEMIC-001 and COURSEWORK-MSC-001 support coursework grounding. Project entries are conditional and individual/team contributions remain unspecified. This establishes relevant academic evidence, not professional Python analytics experience. |
| SQL proficiency for analytics | Partial | SKILL-SQL-001 permits general SQL; CERT-HACKERRANK-001, TRAINING-001 and COURSEWORK-MSC-001 support learning and assessment. PROJ-AZ-MIGRATION establishes report-query changes, but does not specify SQL constructs or independently demonstrate joins, grain and aggregation checks. A concrete personally authored query walkthrough would close the evidence gap. Do not infer database dialects. |
| Dashboard analysis in Tableau, Power BI and/or QuickSight | Supported | PROJ-AZ-EXEC establishes contribution to a three-person Power BI delivery; WORK-HUL-001 establishes enhancements, validation and production-promotion support. PROJ-AZ-MIGRATION adds professional report work; CERT-PL300-001 supports the credential name. Power BI satisfies the listed-tool requirement. PROJ-KPMG-FORAGE offers conditional Tableau evidence from a virtual experience, not KPMG employment. QuickSight is unnecessary to establish this requirement. |
| Basic ML understanding | Supported through academic work | PROJ-MSC-FRAUD demonstrates classification, validation, training-only SMOTE and threshold trade-offs; PROJ-CLUSTERING-DBSCAN demonstrates algorithm implementation and sensitivity analysis; COURSEWORK-MSC-002 supports formal study. Conditional project status and unspecified ownership remain relevant. Weak predictive results do not invalidate evidence of understanding when explained honestly. |
| Data preparation, cleaning and transformation | Supported | PROJ-SECOM-FAULT-DETECTION specifies imputation, feature removal and standardisation; PROJ-FAANG-PCA specifies missing-value checks and leakage precautions. PROJ-AZ-MIGRATION supplies professional Power Query/M transformation work. Academic cleaning and professional BI transformation should retain their separate contexts. |
| Creative problem-solving / innovative thinking | Supported, with an example to substantiate | PROJ-NIQ-POC reports building a reusable finance-dashboard proof of concept from a wireframe; PROJ-AZ-RECON reports co-developed consolidation and source-record drill-through. Both are user-reported professional entries. Explain the problem, alternatives and personal design choices; reported savings are not independently measured. |
| Passion for learning / growth mindset | Supported | PROJ-NIQ-REPORTING records learning a proprietary platform within two weeks; TRAINING-001 records structured training; COURSEWORK-MSC-001 and COURSEWORK-MSC-002 show continued study. A specific example of feedback changing the work would strengthen the growth narrative. |
| Adaptability | Supported | PROJ-NIQ-REPORTING demonstrates rapid platform learning and requirement clarification; PROJ-AZ-MIGRATION demonstrates contribution during a platform transition. Explain personal adjustments without claiming leadership of the migration. |
| Sustainable development / creating a better world | Gap in demonstrated motivation | No active item specifically establishes sustainability motivation or built-environment analysis. PROJ-SECOM-FAULT-DETECTION is an adjacent sensor-data example, but cannot substantiate environmental impact. This is an evidence gap, not proof that the applicant lacks interest. |

The strongest fit is the combination of professional BI delivery and academic analytical methods. PROJ-AZ-EXEC and PROJ-NIQ-REPORTING support communicating with users and handing over outputs; WORK-HUL-001 and WORK-AZ-OTHER-001 support testing. These match the benchmark’s emphasis on useful, validated analysis. Professional data-science tenure is not required, so academic ML evidence is appropriate without relabelling it as employment.

The principal technical uncertainty is demonstrable SQL depth. The other significant weakness is the absence of a concrete sustainability example. Reproducible analytical handover would also benefit from a small reviewable artifact, but it is a desirable evidence standard rather than an additional advertised requirement. More GenAI frameworks, cloud infrastructure or certifications are lower priorities for this role.

No confirmed deal-breaker appears in the supplied profile. Two unresolved matters could become practical blockers:

- Student-placement eligibility: the reported MSc period ends in September 2026, while the placement start date and graduate eligibility are unknown. Relevant completed education alone does not resolve the advert’s “studying” condition.
- Availability and work permission for the actual placement: WORKAUTH-STAMP-001 reports Stamp 1G, and WORKAUTH-001 conditionally reports a visa date of 31 December 2026. Neither establishes permission for an unknown placement period, renewal or future sponsorship. LOCATION-001 establishes Ireland, not Dublin attendance availability.

Questions to resolve before relying on the application narrative:

- What is the current enrolment/completion status, and does Arup accept that status at the placement start date? What are the placement dates and university-placement requirements?
- Can the applicant meet the required hours, Dublin attendance and work-permission requirements for that period?
- Which SQL query can the applicant explain personally, including join cardinality, table grain and reconciliation of totals?
- Which parts of the MSc projects were personally implemented, and which were team contributions? For the fraud capstone, what baseline produced the approximately 26% recall comparison?
- What specific sustainability problem interests the applicant, and what experience or learning supports that interest? What is one example of revising work after feedback?

Three prioritized next actions:

1. Resolve eligibility and reconcile essential facts — approximately 1–2 hours of preparation, plus external response time. Assemble current enrolment/completion information, available dates and relevant permission details; ask the recruiter about placement eligibility and timing. Clarify the exact MSc award title and academic-project ownership. These are proposed checks, not completed confirmations.
2. Package existing evidence and demonstrate SQL — approximately 5–7 hours over several evenings. Select one professional dashboard story and one academic Python/ML example; record the problem, personal contribution, checks and limitations. Using public or synthetic tables, create a small SQL exercise with a join, aggregation and deliberate duplicate-key check, then reconcile its output to Python totals. Produce a short README and practise a five-minute explanation. Use a fresh public-data demonstration where professional artifacts cannot be shared. This would be new practice evidence, not retrospective proof of work done for a client.
3. Complete one small built-environment analysis — approximately 12–18 hours over two weeks. Proposed project: examine electricity consumption for one building over several weeks using licensed public data, or clearly labelled synthetic data if access is impractical. Spend 2–3 hours confirming provenance, units and the decision; 4–5 hours cleaning timestamps and gaps and writing SQL aggregates; 3–4 hours building one Power BI page with coverage and consumption measures; and 3–6 hours validating totals and writing a one-page interpretation. Flag periods for investigation without claiming waste, carbon reductions or achieved savings. A simple chronological baseline comparison is an optional 3–4-hour extension; a complex model is unnecessary. Keep this project labelled proposed or in progress until its milestones are actually completed.

Resume emphasis should lead with professional Power BI/reporting delivery, followed by clearly labelled academic Python and ML evidence. Use the conditional MSc wording above and general SQL; prioritise Power BI, Power Query/M, Python, pandas and scikit-learn over a long GenAI tool list. - “Developed an MSc classification workflow over 10,000 synthetic medical claims, comparing five classifiers with training-only SMOTE and separate validation/test sets.” — PROJ-MSC-FRAUD. Do not imply production readiness or real-world fraud impact.
